ws_findings: All tests run with node18+ws, Origin: https://example.com (accepted — server does not reject cross-origin WS handshakes). (1) BASIC SUBSCRIPTION: send {"action":"want","data":["blocks","stats","mempool-blocks"]}. Server immediately sends one large INIT message (~18.7KB) with keys {blocks, mempool-blocks, mempoolInfo, vBytesPerSecond, fees, da}: `blocks` = last 8 blocks WITH extras (block keys: id,height,version,timestamp,bits,nonce,difficulty,merkle_root,tx_count,size,weight,previousblockhash,mediantime,stale,extras; extras keys incl. reward,coinbaseRaw,medianFee,feeRange,totalFees,avgFee,avgFeeRate,feePercentiles,pool,matchRate,expectedFees,similarity — e.g. {"id":"000000000000000000017eb32057...","height":957515,"tx_count":4485,"extras":{"medianFee":0.8,"feeRange":[0.507,...,1000],"totalFees":1587375,"pool":{...Foundry...}}}). `mempool-blocks` = 8 projected blocks, each {"blockSize":1544055,"blockVSize":997905,"nTx":4904,"totalFees":1312272,"medianFee":0.628,"feeRange":[0.488,0.514,0.514,0.532,1.004,2.011,261.1]} — YES it has feeRange/nTx/totalFees. Then UPDATE messages every ~1.5-1.7s (~3.9KB each, ~2.7KB/s total) with keys {mempoolInfo, vBytesPerSecond, transactions, da, fees, mempool-blocks} — note `transactions` arrives UNREQUESTED: an array of ~6 latest-arrival stubs {"txid":"0cbfcfbb...","fee":112,"vsize":111,"value":15621,"rate":1.009,"time":1783740725}; over 35s it carried 78 unique txids (~2.2/s, with duplicates across updates). `fees` = {"fastestFee":1.129,"halfHourFee":0.774,"hourFee":0.461,"economyFee":0.2,"minimumFee":0.1}. On a new block the server pushes a {"block":{...full block with extras...}} message (shape matches the init `blocks` entries; not captured live in the test window — no block was mined in 25 min of listening — but the init snapshot uses the identical object shape). (2) INDIVIDUAL NEW-TX STREAMS — THE BIG FINDING, both WORK on the public server: {"track-mempool-txids":true} → messages keyed `mempool-txids` = {"sequence":143424,"added":["bfc5e275...","cf19ddfa...","17909..."],"removed":[],"mined":[],"replaced":[]} every ~1.7s; {"track-mempool":true} → messages keyed `mempool-transactions` = same {sequence,added,removed,mined,replaced} envelope but `added` contains FULL transaction objects: keys txid,version,locktime,vin,vout,size,weight,sigops,fee,status,order,vsize,adjustedVsize,feePerVsize,adjustedFeePerVsize,effectiveFeePerVsize,firstSeen,cpfpDirty,clusterId,chunkIndex,cpfpChecked,ancestors,descendants,position,flags — vin[] includes prevout{scriptpubkey,scriptpubkey_asm,scriptpubkey_type,scriptpubkey_address,value}, witness[] (real example: witness:["3045022100fd06e37c...01","03a7a04d5f..."], prevout.scriptpubkey_type:"v0_p2wpkh"), and vout[] includes scriptpubkey_type/address incl. op_return payloads. Measured 64 added txs in 30s (~2.1/s, matching network rate) at ~5.2KB/s bandwidth (quiet mempool; scales with traffic — docs warn "potentially a lot of data", enterprise recommended for guarantees but it WORKS unauthenticated on the public server). When both are subscribed on one connection the server bundles both keys into a single message. `sequence` increments per delta cycle for gap detection. (3) {"action":"want","data":["watch-mempool"]} is silently ignored (not a valid want value; valid: blocks, mempool-blocks, live-2h-chart, stats). "live-2h-chart" want works: one snapshot message {"live-2h-chart":{"added":1783740829,"count":92464,"vbytes_per_second":514,"mempool_byte_weight":175345036,"total_fee":8875404,"min_fee":0.1,"vsizes":[43291711,352641,...]}} (39-bucket vsize histogram). Docs also list track-tx/track-txs, track-address/track-addresses (with max-tracked limits), track-mempool-block (index) for projected-block deltas, and track-rbf.

tx_json_shape: Top level: {txid, version, locktime, vin[], vout[], size, weight, sigops, fee, status}. vin[i] = {txid, vout, prevout: {scriptpubkey, scriptpubkey_asm, scriptpubkey_type, scriptpubkey_address, value}, scriptsig, scriptsig_asm, witness: [hex,...], is_coinbase, sequence}. vout[i] = {scriptpubkey, scriptpubkey_asm, scriptpubkey_type, scriptpubkey_address, value}. Real snippet (txid ec14c4df6e0a772ec8640c9d493deddbbdbe77ccafe664bd0287aa28c8eac649): vin[0].witness = ["304402205d6273bd3d85274ef04bb1be9d633a4e61b2a4179d8f8732d896bb69f22b02c502205b518c82590e88e830b2a3b84273a32d304840906e50e2b760fcd44e6222578501","03c079851ffffa566780c10d7469be4476017a1e7bb592c96054..."], vin[0].prevout.scriptpubkey_type = "v0_p2wpkh"; vout[0] = {"scriptpubkey":"0014c763452890b8a2b56f5d91558d3593c7aa65433c","scriptpubkey_asm":"OP_0 OP_PUSHBYTES_20 c763452890b8a2b56f5d91558d3593c7aa65433c","scriptpubkey_type":"v0_p2wpkh","scriptpubkey_address":"bc1qca3522yshz3t2m6aj92c6dvnc74x2seuqpwgat","value":44303}; status = {"confirmed":false}; fee=856, size=221, weight=557, sigops=1. scriptpubkey_type values observed: v0_p2wpkh, v1_p2tr, op_return (also p2pkh/p2sh/v0_p2wsh per electrs convention). The WS track-mempool `added[]` objects are a SUPERSET of this shape, adding vsize, adjustedVsize, feePerVsize, effectiveFeePerVsize, firstSeen, ancestors, descendants, position, flags (a classification bitmask mempool.space computes server-side).
block_txs_pagination: GET /api/block/:hash/txs returns the first 25 full tx objects (index 0 = coinbase). Next pages use a path segment: /api/block/:hash/txs/25, /txs/50, /txs/75 — each returns up to 25 txs starting at that index. VERIFIED: /txs/25 returns a different set than /txs; the query form ?start_index=25 does NOT work (silently returns page 0 — do not use it); non-multiples of 25 are rejected with HTTP 400 "start index must be a multipication of 25" (sic). Sampling ~100 txs of a block = exactly 4 requests (/txs, /txs/25, /txs/50, /txs/75), ~1.2-1.5MB total JSON for typical blocks. A 4,485-tx block would need 180 requests for full coverage — sample instead.
rate_limits: No numeric limits are published and no X-RateLimit-* / Retry-After headers appear on responses. Official docs (mempool.space/docs/api/rest) state verbatim: "Note that we enforce rate limits. If you exceed these limits, you will get an HTTP 429 error. If you repeatedly exceed the limits, you may be banned from accessing the service altogether." — with enterprise sponsorship (mempool.space/enterprise) suggested for higher limits. Empirically: a burst of 30 parallel GETs to /api/v1/fees/recommended all returned 200 in 275ms with no throttle headers, so casual per-visitor traffic is fine; the limiter is nginx-side per-IP with unpublished thresholds (community reports suggest sustained >~10 req/s per IP risks 429). CORS preflight (OPTIONS) returns 200 with access-control-allow-origin: *, allow-methods GET/POST/PUT/DELETE/OPTIONS. Responses carry cache-control max-age=1 on electrs endpoints. WS connections with a foreign Origin header are accepted. Practical guidance: keep each browser to 1 WS connection + low single-digit REST req/s bursts, and back off on any 429.
recommended_architecture: One WebSocket per visitor, near-zero REST. Verified design: (1) Open wss://mempool.space/api/v1/ws, send {"action":"want","data":["blocks","stats","mempool-blocks"]} AND {"track-mempool":true}. (2) Classifiable tx stream: the `mempool-transactions.added[]` deltas (every ~1.7s) contain FULL transactions — vin[].prevout (script types, values), vin[].witness, vout[].scriptpubkey_type/asm, fee, vsize, effectiveFeePerVsize, even a server-computed `flags` bitmask — so the target 1-3 classifiable tx/s arrives entirely over the socket with ZERO REST calls per tx (at test time the whole network was ~2 tx/s and the stream delivered all of it at ~5KB/s; if a fee spike makes volume excessive, client-side: process only the first N of each `added` batch, or downgrade to {"track-mempool-txids":true} and REST-fetch /api/tx/:txid for a sampled 1-3/s, which stays well under limits). (3) Instant block events: the same socket pushes {"block":{...with extras: totalFees, medianFee, feeRange, pool...}} plus refreshed `mempool-blocks` (projected blocks with nTx/totalFees/feeRange) and `da` — no polling needed; `mempool-transactions.mined[]` even tells you which streamed txs just confirmed. (4) Per-block ~100-tx sampling: on each block event fire exactly 4 sequential REST calls — /api/block/:hash/txs, /txs/25, /txs/50, /txs/75 (path-segment offsets only, multiples of 25) — 4 requests per ~10 minutes is negligible; optionally jitter them 0-30s so simultaneous visitors don't synchronize a thundering herd. (5) Init/refill: /api/v1/blocks (15 blocks WITH extras) on load or WS reconnect; /api/v1/prices 1/min if USD display is wanted; fees/da/mempoolInfo all ride the socket. (6) Resilience: reconnect with exponential backoff + resend subscriptions; use the `sequence` field to detect missed deltas; send {"action":"ping"} every ~30s to keep intermediaries from idling out the socket. Net per-visitor cost: 1 long-lived WS (~3-6KB/s) + ~4 REST calls per block + 1/min price poll — politely inside the public server's tolerances, all CORS-clear (access-control-allow-origin: *) from any static page.
